newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB cuts Australia wheat crop to 14-15 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: AWB cuts Australia wheat crop to 14-15 mln tonnes.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) on Monday cut its estimate of Australia's 1997/98 wheat crop by one million tonnes to between 14 and 15 million tonnes.
The AWB said Australian east coast regions had received very little rain during the past two weeks.
They continued to suffer from frequent and severe frosts, AWB general manager merchandising Ron Storey said in a statement.
"June and July rainfall has been well below average for eastern and southern Australia," Storey said.
AWB could expect to have a 10-11 million tonne export programme against the 18 million tonne programme of 1996/97 as a result of the lower crop, he also said.
The AWB's latest forecast contrasts with the record 1996/97 crop of 23.5 million tonnes and compares with its initial 1997/98 forecast of 18 million tonnes.
A reduction in export availability was exacerbated by higher domestic consumption as wheat was used to supplement domestic feed requirements, he said.
"As a result our prices improve relative to the world market," Storey said.
"We believe that the international market is under-estimating the impact of El Nino in Australia at present and therefore world wheat prices are expected to stabilise or strengthen," he said.
"Certainly domestic prices are unlikely to fall with the production uncertainty in Australia," he said.
The harvesting of the crop would normally start in the northernmost wheatbelt region of central Queensland in October and peak elsewhere in December-January.

El Nino is a weather pattern, caused by warm sea surface temperatures off South America and their interaction with the atmosphere, which causes drought in eastern Australia, Indonesia and nearby areas.
